taxonomyNote: That review lists synonyms Capra hircus aegagrus and Capra aegagrus hircus; NatureServe describes C. hircus as the domestic form of C. aegagrus.
fieldMarks: Straight prominent horns (larger on males), rectangular pupils, coarse hair
Usually 25-55 kg, 1-1.2 m at the shoulder, 1-1.5 m long; males about 20% larger
All males and some females are bearded; short, upward-pointing tail distinguishes goats from sheep
Coat usually black, but white, grey, brown, red or any combination occurs
behavior: Herds with a modal group size of two to four; up to 100 not uncommon, groups up to 200 recorded in Hawaii
Three herd types: all-male bachelor herds, mixed-sex groups, and females with young
Generalist herbivores taking grasses, forbs and browse
Excellent eyesight with a 320-340 degree field of view
habitat: Rugged mountain country, rocky crags and alpine meadows; survive on a wide variety of forage with limited water.
range: Feral populations occur on islands worldwide, including Hawaii and California's San Clemente Island; NatureServe records the species (Capra hircus) as present in Hawaii, New Mexico and California.

lookalikes.name: Feral sheep
lookalikes.howToTell: Goats have short, upward-pointing tails, which sheep lack (Pacific Science review).

lookalikes.name: Persian ibex
lookalikes.howToTell: Wild ancestor species; sources read give no field mark separating it from feral goats.
